title: Platform operator runway and cross-team onboarding compact
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This compact defines the concept of an "operator runway" (lead time and readiness for platform operators), describes a prescriptive cross-team onboarding flow, and collects the minimum dashboards, alerts, and runbook steps an operator must own before being signed off for independent shifts. The goal is consistent operator readiness across regions and teams while keeping the process lean and measurable.

Why an operator runway?
- Platform operators at Redwood are asked to make rapid, high‑impact decisions across the serving runtime, routing, and tenant isolation surfaces.
- The runway model sets a predictable lead time for training, instrumentation, and scoped autonomy so we reduce incident churn and cognitive load.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: new and existing Platform Operators, SREs transitioning to platform oncall, and first‑line engineering incident responders.
- Scope: inference-serving infra (regional controller, batch router, KV/prefix cache), tenant priority slices, and platform-sidecar contracts. Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks.

Operator runway definition (observable milestones):
1) Day 0 — Access & Tools (Target lead time: 2 business days)
   - Slack: access to #platform-ops and region-specific channels (e.g., #platform-ops-eu1).
   - PagerDuty: added to the Platform oncall escalation policy with correct escalation path.
   - IAM: ability to read logs and dashboards, escalate tickets, and open emergency HA tickets.
2) Day 3 — Core dashboards and telemetry (Target lead time: 5 business days)
   - Familiar with the Platform Overview dashboard and the Runway Health tile.
   - Able to read token-cost, tail-latency, and KV cache hit-rate panels.
3) Week 1 — Runbooks and standard procedures (Target lead time: 10 business days)
   - Can execute cold-start warmup and prefix cache shard rebalance runbooks with a senior observer.
   - Completes the example safe rollback exercise in a staging region.
4) Week 3 — Independent incident handling (Target lead time: 21 business days)
   - Triage incidents to SLO, cost, or security buckets and run the appropriate mitigation flow.
   - Demonstrates canary and automatic-fallback activation on a simulated degradation.

Onboarding flow (step-by-step):
1) Preflight (people-ops + onboarding buddy)
   - Verify access, schedule 1:1 with regional tech lead, and assign onboarding buddy.
2) Shadow week (days 1–5)
   - Observe two live shift rotations and review the last three postmortems.
   - Complete the Runway checklist: items are ticked on the checklist doc.
3) Guided exercises (week 2)
   - Execute: cache warmup, model-swap simulation, and burst-surge mitigation in staging.
   - Dashboard task: create an annotated runbook trace for a synthetic tail-latency incident.
4) Signoff (week 3)
   - Buddy and tech lead approve operator readiness via a short practical exam: triage + mitigation within SLO targets.

Minimum dashboards and panels (must be present and understood):
- Platform Overview (single pane)
   - Graphs: regional request rate (rps), p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate by model version.
- Runway Health tile (for shift handoff)
   - KV cache hit-rate (3m window), token burst across top 10 tenants, current autoscaler headroom.
- Cost & Token attribution
   - Rolling 24h token spend by tenant, unusual spend anomaly sparkline.
- Degradation lab (synthetic lab panel)
   - Canary success rate, prefix-cache-eviction events, cold-start queue length.

Example panel queries (PromQL):
- p99 latency: 100 * histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, job))
- KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Token spend spike detector (simple): increase(token_spend_total[1h]) > 5 * avg_over_time(increase(token_spend_total[6h])[6h:1h])

Minimum alerts and thresholds (operator should understand intent and playbook):
- Platform-degradation-critical (SEV0): p99 latency > 2s for 3m AND error rate > 2% for 5m. PagerDuty: platform-sev0.
- KV-cache-eviction-surge (SEV1): eviction-rate > 100 evictions/m for 5m. Slack: #platform-ops, P0 runbook.
- Token-cost-anomaly (SEV2): tenant token spend > 3x baseline within 30m. Slack alert to #cost-alerts and ops-notes.
- Autoscaler-starvation (SEV1): available GPU headroom < 10% AND pending request queue > 50 for 10m. Trigger runbook for hybrid-burst-policy.

Operator runbooks & quick procedures (links to canonical runbooks)
- Emergency model swap and token surge mitigation: steps to cut model variant weights, enable cheaper quantized variant, and apply tenant throttles.
- KV prefix-cache rebalancing: preflight checks, dry-run rebalance command, live rebalancing steps, and validation queries.
- Cold-start warmup orchestration: phased warmup commands and safety gate checks (see example CLI below).

Example CLI snippets (staging)
- Dry-run cache rebalance: redwoodctl cache rebalance --region eu1 --dry-run --max-move 10
- Promote fallback model: redwoodctl model set-weight --model rwd-quant-3b --weight 0.8 --target-tenants t123,t456

Operator handoff template (what to cover in a 10-minute handoff):
1) Current incidents and status (links to incident tickets).
2) Anything scheduled that affects runway (maintenance, model rollouts).
3) Known noisy tenants or experiments.
4) Actions to pick up if alerts fire and owner for each.

Emergency runway (fast-activation path)
- When a region crosses the emergency threshold (loss of >30% serving capacity for 15m):
  1) Activate emergency operator runway: enable cross-region failover as per the failover DSL.
  2) Notify Product and Customer Success for impacted customers.
  3) Record to the Timeline and start the post-incident retro template within 48h.

Signoff & certification criteria (ticklist used during signoff):
- Access and tools verified.
- Confirmed ability to read and interpret the Platform Overview dashboard.
- Performed a successful dry-run cache rebalance in staging.
- Demonstrated safe rollback of a canary deployment.
- Completed the practical incident triage within SLOs.

Ownership matrix (quick reference):
| Area | Primary owner | Secondary | Signoff required |
|------|---------------|-----------|-----------------|
| KV cache health | runtime-engineering | platform-ops | runtime-eng lead |
| Autoscaler config | infra-scaling | platform-ops | infra-scaling owner |
| Token attribution | cost-engineering | platform-ops | cost-eng manager |
| Dashboards | observability | platform-ops | observability lead |

How retrospectives feed the runway and roadmap:
- Trigger conditions for a short retro (operator-led): any SEV1 incident impacting >1 region or recurring SEV2 pattern within 30 days.
- Outcome artifacts: runbook delta, dashboard panel added/updated, and a follow-up ticket on the platform roadmap with clear success criteria.

Measuring runway health (quarterly signals):
- Mean lead time to operator signoff (target: <= 21 business days).
- Number of postmortems where operator readiness was cited as contributing factor (target: 0).
- Fraction of oncalls passing the practical exam on first attempt (target: >= 85%).

Appendix: common links and resources
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/
- Dashboards: Grafana -> Platform Overview -> Runway Health
- Oncall exam: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-onboarding-certification-pathway-2026.json
- Slack channels: #platform-ops, #platform-ops-eu1, #cost-alerts

If you are a new operator: start by bookmarking the Runway Health tile, schedule your signoff with your buddy, and run the dry‑run exercises in staging before attempting a production change.
